diagnostic_evidence.quote: We perform a rigorous convergence analysis of our algorithm to show that it converges to the true $\CW_2$-barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ in an almost sure sense (see Setting~\ref{sett: convergence} and Theorem~\ref{thm: fixedpoint-convergence}).

In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$.
However, to the best of our knowledge, sufficient conditions to guarantee the uniqueness of the fixed-point of~$G$ for non-parametric $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ is still an open problem.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contribution (ii) assert that the algorithm is provably convergent (a.s.) to the $\CW_2$-barycenter for continuous non-parametric input measures. What is actually established (Theorem 3) is a.s. precompactness with all accumulation points being fixed points of $G$, plus convergence to the barycenter only under the extra hypothesis that $G$ has a unique fixed point. That hypothesis is not part of Setting 1/2, is acknowledged in the paper's own remark to be open for non-parametric inputs, and $G$ can have multiple fixed points even for absolutely continuous inputs (the paper itself cites a counterexample), in which case the proven accumulation-at-fixed-points guarantee does not identify the limit as the barycenter. The prose therefore claims more than the formal content supports.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the abstract and contribution (ii) to state the actual guarantee: a.s. accumulation at fixed points of $G$, and convergence to the barycenter when $G$ has a unique fixed point.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised headline guarantee (a.s. convergence to the barycenter for general non-parametric measures) is not established by the paper; only the weaker conditional guarantee is.
issues.title: Headline prose claims unconditional a.s. convergence to the barycenter
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local prose rewording; no theorem, algorithm, or formal guarantee is lost or weakened.

issues.failure_explanation: Setting 2 defines $\widehat R_t$ through the functions $\overline r_1,\overline r_2$ supplied by Lemma 2 and asserts $\CF_t$-measurability. Lemma 2, however, only asserts existence of $\overline r_1,\overline r_2$ as functions that 'depend on' their arguments, with no Borel-dependence property; by contrast, Assumption 2(iii) explicitly demands Borel dependence for the analogous selection functions $\overline n,\widetilde\theta$, showing the paper elsewhere recognizes this requirement. Since $\widehat\rho_t$ is a random measure, without measurable selections the random variable $\widehat R_t$ (hence $\widehat\mu_t$, $\widehat N_{t,k}$, $\widehat\Theta_{t,k}$, the filtration construction, and the conditional-expectation steps in Theorem 3) is not well founded as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Lemma 2 to supply Borel-measurable selections (e.g., canonical minimal $r$'s, using continuity of $\rho\mapsto\CW_2(\rho|_{\CX_r},\rho)$ and the assumed Borel dependences of the estimator), so that $\widehat R_t$ as defined in Setting 2 is genuinely $\CF_t$-measurable.
issues.overall_effect: The adapted-process framework of Setting 2 and the filtration-based convergence proofs of Theorem 3 and Corollary 5 rest on an unestablished measurability property of the truncation selections.
issues.title: Measurability of the truncation index $\widehat R_t$ is asserted but not established
issues.why_classification: The gap is closed by a contained, standard measurable-selection argument; every statement, guarantee, and proof step survives with unchanged substance.

issues.failure_explanation: Statement (iii) of Proposition 3 asserts the displayed risk bound for all sample sizes down to the stated lower bounds ($\underline m=1$, and $n$ down to its printed lower bound) and all $0<\theta\le\overline\theta$. The proof derives it from the cited Pooladian--Niles-Webb result only for $m\ge2$, $n\ge2$ (as its in-proof display states), and the simplified form only for $m,n\ge7$; nothing covers $m=1$. There the claim is false: with a single source sample, the dual first-order conditions force $g_j=\frac12\|X_1-Y_j\|^2-f_1$, so the estimator becomes a softmax with weights proportional to $\exp(\langle Y_j,x-X_1\rangle/\theta)$; as $n\to\infty$ and $\theta\to0$ it degenerates to a boundary-point map of $\conv\{Y_j\}$ and its $\CL^2(\mu)$-error stays bounded away from $0$ (e.g., $\mu=\nu$ uniform on a convex body), while the right-hand side, in which $\log(m)m^{-1/2}=\log(1)=0$, tends to $0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the displayed bound in Proposition 3(iii) to $m\ge2$ (equivalently set $\underline m:=2$); the Assumption 2(iii) verification via $\overline n\ge7$ and all downstream uses are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated parameter regime of the consistency bound in Proposition 3(iii) is unreliable at $m=1$. The subsequent 'In particular' verification of Assumption 2(iii) (which uses $\overline n\ge\max\{d+1,7,\ldots\}\ge7$) and all downstream results are unaffected.
issues.title: Entropic estimator risk bound asserted from $m\ge\underline m=1$ but only established (and valid) for $m\ge2$
issues.why_classification: A one-line regime correction (or setting $\underline m:=2$) preserves the estimator's admissibility, the consistency verification, and every downstream claim; only an unproven (and false) edge regime of one displayed bound is withdrawn.

Proposition 3, however, is stated and proved only for $q\ge1$: its consistency analysis uses $q+2\ge3$ (Lipschitz Hessian, finiteness of the Fisher-information term $I_0$) and asserts $3\le\overline\alpha(\mu,\nu)\le4$, which fails for $q=0$. Thus for $q=0$ inputs the estimator's Assumption 2(iii) property, on which the corollary's proof relies, is not established, and the corollary's claimed regime exceeds what its supporting results prove.
